item.title: McGregor won't be part of fight night at White House
item.description: UFC president Dana White has confirmed that Conor McGregor won't be part of their fight night at the White House in June. Former two-weight world champion McGregor had claimed that he was preparing to make his comeback on the card. He hasn't fought since losing to Dustin Poirier in their trilogy bout in 2021. item.title: Waterford v Tipperary to be played this Sunday
item.description: The re-fixed National Hurling League Division One A match between Waterford and Tipperary will be played at Walsh Park this Sunday afternoon. A loss for the Deise against the All-Ireland champions would see them make a swift return to Division One B. There will be a 2pm throw-in. Advertisement

item.title: No fresh injury concerns for Scotland
item.description: Ireland have no fresh injury concerns ahead of their final Six Nations match against Scotland this weekend. Loosehead prop Jeremy Loughman remains sidelined with a calf injury, and Connacht's Billy Bohan has come in as cover. Munster forward Brian Gleeson has also linked with the group and will train with the squad this week. item.title: Judge jails man for ten months for “almost farcical” attempt at robbing Tralee bookies
item.description: A homeless man has been jailed for ten months for what a judge called an almost farcical attempt at robbing a bookies in Tralee. Tralee Circuit Court was told 47-year-old John Paul Farrell, who had been residing at a homeless hostel in Killarney, was highly intoxicated during the incident. Mr Farrell wore a balaclava, but was identified by an eagle-eyed garda who noticed he was missing a finger similar to the man captured on the bookies’ CCTV. item.title: Michael Fassbender portrait goes missing in Killarney town centre
item.description: A piece of street art featuring a portrait of actor Michael Fassbender has gone missing in Killarney. The likeness was painted on an electricity power box, and had been standing close to the court house at East Avenue Road, until it disappeared over the weekend. It was done in collaboration with Kerry County Council and an art initiative called GRAFT in the centre of Killarney town.
